Definition: apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern):--move, quake, shake.
BiblicalUsage: Seio is shaking, and it shakes the earth and the city. The voice that shook the earth at Sinai will yet once more shake not the earth only, but also heaven. And when Jesus came into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that the same shaking falls on both: the earth shook at His voice, and the city shook at His coming.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
